angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 395,853 km at 46.50 pc = 0.11 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 21.5051 +/- 0.0111 mas (same row, RUWE 0.86): 46.50 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.569 +/- 0.02 solar radii from Geraldía-González et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of Ross 176 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...700A.216G/abstract): 395,853 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.577 +/- 0.024 solar masses from Geraldía-González et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of Ross 176 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...700A.216G/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4041 +/- 69 K from Geraldía-González et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Ross 176 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...700A.216G/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Geraldía-González et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Ross 176 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...700A.216G/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/ross-176.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.689, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
